'''Kōtoku-ji''' (広徳寺, こうとくじ) is a {{ill|Tendai|ja|天台宗|lt=Tendai|lt_ja=天台宗}} Buddhist temple at Yamagami, Minakuchi-chō, {{ill|Kōka, Shiga|ja|甲賀市|lt=Kōka|lt_ja=甲賀市}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ja|滋賀県|lt=Shiga Prefecture|lt_ja=滋賀県}}. Its {{ill|Sangō|ja|山号|lt=mountain name|lt_ja=山号}} is Kōshinzan, and its {{ill|Honzon|ja|本尊|lt=principal image|lt_ja=本尊}} is {{ill|Shōmen Kongō|ja|青面金剛|lt=Shōmen Kongō|lt_ja=青面金剛尊}}.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kōka Shishi, vol. 8: Kōka-shi Jiten|date=12 December 2016|year=2016|publisher=Kōka City|page=72}}</ref> It is popularly called "the Kōshin-san (of Yamagami)".

According to the temple's tradition, in {{ill|783|ja|783年|lt=783|lt_ja=783年}} ({{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|lt=Enryaku|lt_ja=延暦}} 2), when {{ill|Saichō|ja|最澄|lt=Saichō|lt_ja=最澄}} came here looking for timber to build Enryaku-ji, he saw a light shining on the summit with purple clouds trailing over it. Climbing to the top, he saw lightning strike from a rock more than a ''jō'' high, and within it perceived the sacred form of the great Shōmen Kongō; he carved an image himself and enshrined it, and that is said to be the temple's beginning. From the Edo period on it drew the devotion of people in the brass trade, as the place of brass's founder.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kindai Nihon no Shindōgyō: Suisha kara Umareta Kinzoku Kakō|date=2008-12-12|publisher={{ill|Sangyo Shimbun|ja|産業新聞社|lt=Sangyō Shimbunsha|lt_ja=産業新聞社}}|pages=32–34|isbn=4990231341}}</ref>

In {{ill|1616|ja|1616年|lt=1616|lt_ja=1616年}} ({{ill|Genna|ja|元和 (日本)|lt=Genna|lt_ja=元和}} 2), Tōzaemon of Yamagami village (see below) rebuilt the halls. On 22 April {{ill|2013|ja|2013年|lt=2013|lt_ja=2013年}} the main hall burned down in a fire caused by an electrical fault; it was rebuilt by the end of March {{ill|2017|ja|2017年|lt=2017|lt_ja=2017年}}.

It has been chosen as "View over the village of Kōka" among the {{ill|Deai Kōka Hakkei|ja|であい・こうか八景|lt=Deai Kōka eight views|lt_ja=であい・こうか八景}}, Kōka City's attractive landscapes, and as "Autumn colours of Kōshin" among the Minakuchi eight tourist views of the former {{ill|Minakuchi, Shiga|ja|水口町|lt=Minakuchi|lt_ja=水口町}}. There is an observation platform with a wide view over Kōka City, and the temple is known for its autumn leaves.<ref name=":0" />

== Faith connected with brass ==
A legend about the founder of brass is handed down here.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|title=Kindai Nihon no Shindōgyō: Suisha kara Umareta Kinzoku Kakō|date=2008-12-12|publisher={{ill|Sangyo Shimbun|ja|産業新聞社|lt=Sangyō Shimbunsha|lt_ja=産業新聞社}}|isbn=4990231341|pages=26–27}}</ref> Tōzaemon of Yamagami village at the foot of the mountain was a poor farmer who could barely make a living. Deeply devoted to the principal image, Shōmen Kongō, he shut himself in Kōtoku-ji to pray at New Year in {{ill|1593|ja|1593年|lt=1593|lt_ja=1593年}} ({{ill|Bunroku|ja|文禄|lt=Bunroku|lt_ja=文禄}} 2). On a full-moon night he was taught the method of alloying copper with zinc, and in {{ill|1599|ja|1599年|lt=1599|lt_ja=1599年}} ({{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|lt=Keichō|lt_ja=慶長}} 4) he tried it in Kyoto and succeeded in making {{ill|Brass|ja|黄銅|lt=brass|lt_ja=真鍮}}.<ref name=":1" /> Until then, substitutes for gold and ornaments had been pure gold, or copper or bronze {{ill|Plating|ja|めっき|lt=plated|lt_ja=メッキ}} with gold; brass did not flake or discolour, nor did copper's green patina appear, so it came into wide use, and the method was a breakthrough.<ref name=":1" /> It is thought, however, that he did not develop it himself but improved a method that had come from the continent.<ref name=":1" />

Hoping to share in this success story, metalware dealers of the {{ill|Santo|ja|三都|lt=three capitals|lt_ja=三都}}, Edo, Kyoto and Osaka, worshipped here in the Edo period as the "originator of brass" and "ancestral god of brass". In {{ill|1851|ja|1851年|lt=1851|lt_ja=1851年}} ({{ill|Kaei|ja|嘉永|lt=Kaei|lt_ja=嘉永}} 4) the metalware dealers of the three capitals set up many stone signposts around the foot of the mountain. Best known is the signpost with the three monkeys "see no evil, speak no evil, hear no evil" beside {{ill|Japan National Route 307|ja|国道307号|lt=National Route 307|lt_ja=国道307号}} at Ushikai,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kōshinzan Kōtoku-ji three-monkey stone signpost|url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/388238|website=Bunka Isan Online|accessdate=2020-06-05|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|ja|文化庁|lt=Agency for Cultural Affairs|lt_ja=文化庁}}}}</ref> set up at the initiative of Chōzaburō, eighth head of the Mitani family of the Kinokuniya, with five Kyoto wholesalers as organisers.<ref name=":0" /> More than a hundred {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|lt=tamagaki|lt_ja=玉垣}} (stone fence posts) were donated, and they are said to cover almost everyone in the brass trade across the country at that time.<ref name=":0" /> The Mitani family of the Kinokuniya gave the most, nine with their associates, and also donated a ''jōyatō'' lantern among other things.<ref name=":0" /> From the Taishō period support from the Osaka brass trade grew. In {{ill|1922|ja|1922年|lt=1922|lt_ja=1922年}} ({{ill|Taishō|ja|大正|lt=Taishō|lt_ja=大正}} 11), Sakane Buhei IV, head of the Osaka brass association, whose base was a Kōshin confraternity, called on brass makers across the country to form the Yamagami Kōshin-dō Preservation Society, which held commemorative events and put up a bronze statue of Tōzaemon.<ref name=":0" /> The statue was given up for metal during the war and rebuilt after it.<ref name=":0" />
